functions.name: fread
functions.signature: size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Reads up to nmemb items of data, each of size bytes, from the given FILE stream into the buffer pointed to by ptr. Returns the number of whole items successfully read. Typical usage: buffered binary/text input where short reads are possible; callers should check the return value and use feof()/ferror() on the stream to distinguish EOF from error.
requirements: ptr must be a valid pointer to a writable buffer of at least size * nmemb bytes when nmemb and size are nonzero.
stream must be a valid FILE* opened for reading.
If size or nmemb is zero, the function performs no read and returns 0.
Partial reads can occur; callers must handle return values less than nmemb and check feof(stream) and ferror(stream) to determine the cause.
The function does not NUL-terminate data; callers must manage any termination if treating data as strings.
Behavior is undefined if ptr is NULL and size*nmemb > 0 or if stream is invalid/closed.

functions.name: fwrite
functions.signature: size_t fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Writes up to nmemb items of data, each of size bytes, from the buffer pointed to by ptr to the given FILE stream. Returns the number of whole items successfully written. Typical usage: buffered binary/text output; callers should handle partial writes by checking the return value and using ferror() on the stream.
requirements: ptr must be a valid pointer to a readable buffer of at least size * nmemb bytes when nmemb and size are nonzero.
stream must be a valid FILE* opened for writing (or read/update modes that allow writing).
If size or nmemb is zero, the function performs no write and returns 0.
Partial writes can occur; callers must handle return values less than nmemb and check ferror(stream) for errors.
Flushing or closing the stream may be required to ensure data reaches the underlying device; callers should use fflush()/fclose() as appropriate.
Behavior is undefined if ptr is NULL and size*nmemb > 0 or if stream is invalid/closed.

functions.name: strcasecmp
functions.description: Performs a case-insensitive comparison of the two C strings s1 and s2, returning an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if s1 is found, respectively, to be less than, to match, or be greater than s2 in a case-insensitive lexicographical order. Typical usage: case-insensitive string equality or ordering checks.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be pointers to valid, NUL-terminated strings.
The function reads both strings until a difference is found or a terminating NUL is encountered; both pointers must reference accessible memory up to and including their NUL terminators.
Return value must be checked for sign (<0, 0, >0); exact magnitude is not specified.
Comparison semantics may be locale-dependent on some platforms; callers should ensure locale expectations if ordering matters.

functions.name: strncasecmp
functions.signature: int strncasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n);
functions.description: Performs a case-insensitive comparison of at most n bytes of the C strings s1 and s2. Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if, within the first n bytes, s1 is found to be less than, to match, or be greater than s2 in a case-insensitive lexicographical order. Typical usage: bounded, case-insensitive comparisons to avoid scanning entire strings.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be pointers to valid, NUL-terminated strings or to character arrays with at least n accessible bytes; the function may stop earlier if a NUL is encountered.
n is the maximum number of bytes to compare; if n is 0, the function returns 0 without accessing s1 or s2.
Return value must be checked for sign (<0, 0, >0); exact magnitude is not specified.
Comparison semantics may be locale-dependent on some platforms; callers should ensure locale expectations if ordering matters.

functions.name: curl_url
functions.description: Create a new CURLU URL handle for libcurl's URL API. Use it to set or get URL components via curl_url_set and curl_url_get. The returned handle must be released with curl_url_cleanup when no longer needed.
requirements: Caller must release the returned CURLU* with curl_url_cleanup().
Do not assume this call frees or manages any strings previously obtained from other APIs; it only creates a handle.
Thread-safety/allocator details are not specified here; use per the libcurl URL API conventions.

functions.name: curl_url_cleanup
functions.description: Free a CURLU handle and all resources associated with the handle's URL parsing state. It does not free strings previously returned by the URL API.
requirements: handle must be a CURLU* previously obtained from curl_url() or curl_url_dup().
Strings allocated and returned by curl_url_get() must be freed separately with curl_free(); curl_url_cleanup() will not free them.
Passing NULL is not documented; behavior is unknown.

functions.name: curl_url_dup
functions.description: Duplicate an existing CURLU handle, producing an independent copy that can be modified separately. The duplicated handle must be freed with curl_url_cleanup.
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized CURLU* returned by curl_url() or previously duplicated.
Caller must free the returned CURLU* with curl_url_cleanup().
Exact duplication semantics (deep vs. shallow) beyond producing a usable independent handle are not further documented here.

functions.name: curl_url_get
functions.signature: CURL_EXTERN CURLUcode curl_url_get(const CURLU *handle, CURLUPart what, char **part, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Extract a specific component or the full URL from a CURLU handle. On success, assigns an allocated NUL-terminated string to *part that the caller must free with curl_free(). Behavior can be adjusted via flags (bitwise OR of CURLU_* defines, e.g., CURLU_URLDECODE, CURLU_DEFAULT_PORT, CURLU_PUNYCODE). Returns a CURLUcode indicating success or the type of error.
requirements: handle must be a valid CURLU*.
what must be a valid CURLUPart selector (e.g., CURLUPART_SCHEME, CURLUPART_HOST, CURLUPART_URL, etc.).
part must be a non-NULL pointer to char*; on success it will receive an allocated string that must be freed with curl_free().
flags is a bitmask of CURLU_* options defined in this header; use 0 for default behavior.
Caller must check the returned CURLUcode and handle errors appropriately before using *part.
Returned string ownership is always the caller’s; free with curl_free() exactly once.

functions.name: curl_url_set
functions.signature: CURL_EXTERN CURLUcode curl_url_set(CURLU *handle, CURLUPart what, const char *part, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Set or clear a specific URL component in a CURLU handle. The input string is copied into the handle. Passing NULL for part clears that component. Behavior can be adjusted via flags (bitwise OR of CURLU_* defines, e.g., CURLU_URLENCODE, CURLU_APPENDQUERY, CURLU_DISALLOW_USER). Returns a CURLUcode indicating success or the type of error.
requirements: handle must be a valid CURLU*.
what must be a valid CURLUPart selector for the component to set or clear.
If part is non-NULL, it must point to a valid NUL-terminated string; its contents are copied by the function.
If part is NULL, the specified component is cleared.
flags is a bitmask of CURLU_* options defined in this header; use 0 for default behavior.
Caller must check the returned CURLUcode and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: curl_url_strerror
functions.description: Convert a CURLUcode error value to a human-readable string suitable for diagnostics and logging. Useful for printing meaningful error messages after curl_url_get or curl_url_set failures.
requirements: Argument must be a valid CURLUcode value.
Returned pointer refers to a constant string managed by the library; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: curl_easy_header
functions.description: Query a specific HTTP header from a libcurl easy handle by name and index. Returns a CURLHcode status and, on success, sets *hout to an internal struct curl_header describing the matched header instance. Typically used after a transfer has produced headers; can also be used to query different header sets (regular headers, trailers, CONNECT, 1xx, or pseudo headers) via the origin flag and a specific request number in case of redirects or multiple requests.
requirements: easy must be a valid CURL easy handle obtained from curl_easy_init and not already freed.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string naming the header field to look up. (Inferred from parameter type and typical usage; the header does not state behavior for NULL.)

index must be a 0-based non-negative size_t selecting which occurrence of the named header to return (e.g., index=0 for the first). (Inferred from the struct curl_header comment: index is 0 or higher.)
origin must be a bit flag selecting the header set; use one of: CURLH_HEADER, CURLH_TRAILER, CURLH_CONNECT, CURLH_1XX, or CURLH_PSEUDO. (Derived from the provided 'origin' bits defines.)
request must be a non-negative int selecting the request number; if the handle has not performed that many requests, the function may return CURLHE_NOREQUEST. (Derived from CURLHE_NOREQUEST.)
hout must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result on success; only dereference *hout if the function returns CURLHE_OK.

Check the return value; on success it is CURLHE_OK. Possible error codes include CURLHE_BADINDEX, CURLHE_MISSING, CURLHE_NOHEADERS, CURLHE_NOREQUEST, CURLHE_OUT_OF_MEMORY, CURLHE_BAD_ARGUMENT, CURLHE_NOT_BUILT_IN. (From the CURLHcode enum.)
The struct curl_header and its fields are owned by libcurl; do not modify or free them. Lifetime relative to the easy handle is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown here.

functions.name: curl_easy_nextheader
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN struct curl_header *curl_easy_nextheader(CURL *easy,
                                                     unsigned int origin,
                                                     int request,
                                                     struct curl_header *prev);
functions.description: Iterate over headers for a given easy handle, origin set, and request number. Pass prev as NULL to get the first header; then pass the previously returned pointer to get the next one, until NULL is returned. Useful for enumerating all headers (or trailers, CONNECT, 1xx, pseudo) associated with a particular request.
requirements: easy must be a valid CURL easy handle obtained from curl_easy_init and not already freed.
origin must select which header set to iterate: one of CURLH_HEADER, CURLH_TRAILER, CURLH_CONNECT, CURLH_1XX, or CURLH_PSEUDO. (Derived from the provided 'origin' bits defines.)

request must be a non-negative int selecting the request number; if no such request exists, iteration yields NULL. (Inferred from the presence of CURLHE_NOREQUEST in related API; this function itself does not return an error code.)

prev must be either NULL (to start iteration) or a pointer previously returned by this function for the same easy handle, origin, and request. Do not pass a pointer from another handle or modify the struct.
The returned pointer is NULL when there are no (more) headers to iterate or on failure; callers must check for NULL to end iteration.
The returned struct curl_header is owned by libcurl; do not modify or free it. Its lifetime relative to the easy handle is not specified in this header and is therefore unknown here.

functions.name: curl_easy_option_by_name
functions.description: Looks up metadata for a libcurl easy option by its option name string (e.g., "CURLOPT_URL"). Returns a pointer to a const curl_easyoption descriptor on success, or NULL if no such option exists. Typical usage: introspection, validation, or tooling that needs type/flag information for curl_easy_setopt options. The returned object is immutable and owned by libcurl.
requirements: Argument name must point to a valid, null-terminated C string representing an option name (for example, "CURLOPT_URL").
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect an unknown/unsupported option name.
The returned pointer refers to static, const data owned by libcurl; the caller must not modify or free it.
This function performs a lookup only; it does not validate or set option values on an easy handle.

functions.name: curl_easy_option_by_id
functions.description: Looks up metadata for a libcurl easy option by its CURLoption id (e.g., CURLOPT_URL). Returns a pointer to a const curl_easyoption descriptor on success, or NULL if no such option id exists in this libcurl build. Useful for mapping ids to expected types/flags before calling curl_easy_setopt.
requirements: Argument id should be a CURLoption value; passing an unknown/unsupported id results in a NULL return.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect an unknown/unsupported option id.
The returned pointer refers to static, const data owned by libcurl; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: curl_easy_option_next
functions.description: Iterates over all supported libcurl easy options and returns descriptors one by one. Pass NULL to obtain the first option; pass the previously returned pointer to get the next. Returns NULL when there are no more options. Enables enumeration of all options and their types/flags.
requirements: Argument prev must be either NULL (to start iteration) or a pointer previously returned by curl_easy_option_next, curl_easy_option_by_name, or curl_easy_option_by_id.
Caller must iterate until the function returns NULL to detect the end of the list.
The returned pointer refers to static, const data owned by libcurl; the caller must not modify or free it.
Do not pass arbitrary or fabricated pointers as prev.

functions.name: curl_easy_init
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new easy session handle for libcurl transfers. Typically used as the first call in an easy API workflow before setting options and performing a transfer. If allocation fails, the return may be NULL (exact failure behavior not stated here). Call curl_easy_cleanup() when done with the handle.
requirements: Must be called before using the handle with other easy functions such as curl_easy_setopt(), curl_easy_perform(), etc.
The returned handle must later be passed to curl_easy_cleanup() to free associated resources.
Do not use the handle if initialization failed (e.g., if a NULL is returned).

functions.name: curl_easy_setopt
functions.description: Sets an option on an easy session handle. The variadic value(s) must match the type required by the specified CURLoption. Typically called multiple times after curl_easy_init() to configure a transfer (URL, callbacks, timeouts, etc.).
requirements: curl must point to a valid CURL easy handle (e.g., from curl_easy_init() or curl_easy_duphandle()).
The variadic argument(s) following option MUST be of the specific type required by that option; passing an incorrect type is invalid.
Should be called before curl_easy_perform() to configure the transfer.
Check the returned CURLcode; only proceed if it indicates success.

functions.name: curl_easy_perform
functions.description: Performs a blocking transfer as configured on the easy handle by previous curl_easy_setopt() calls. Returns a CURLcode indicating success or failure.
requirements: curl must point to a valid, properly configured CURL easy handle.
All required options for the intended transfer must have been set via curl_easy_setopt() prior to calling.
Check and handle the returned CURLcode; subsequent operations may depend on successful completion.

functions.name: curl_easy_cleanup
functions.description: Frees an easy session handle and releases associated resources. Call when the handle is no longer needed.
requirements: curl must be a handle obtained from curl_easy_init() or curl_easy_duphandle().
After this call, the handle becomes invalid and must not be used again.

functions.name: curl_easy_getinfo
functions.description: Retrieves internal information about a session/transfer. The third argument must be a pointer to a variable of the specific type required by the info option. Intended to be used after a performed transfer; results are undefined until the transfer completes. The pointed-to data is valid only if the function returns CURLE_OK.
requirements: curl must be a valid CURL easy handle.
The third argument MUST be a pointer to the specific type required by the given CURLINFO option.
Only rely on the filled-in data if the function returns CURLE_OK.
Intended to be called after a completed transfer; results are undefined before the transfer is completed.

functions.name: curl_easy_duphandle
functions.description: Creates and returns a new easy handle with the same options as the given handle. It clones options but not internal state like active connections; persistent connections and similar runtime state are not transferred. Useful for preparing per-thread handles without reapplying all options.
requirements: curl must be a valid CURL easy handle with options set to be duplicated.
Call curl_easy_cleanup() on the returned handle when finished with it.
Do not assume internal state (e.g., persistent connections) is copied; only options are duplicated.

functions.name: curl_easy_reset
functions.description: Re-initializes an easy handle to its default option values, effectively returning it to the post-creation state while keeping live connections, the Session ID cache, the DNS cache, and cookies intact.
requirements: curl must be a valid CURL easy handle.
After reset, any options previously set (except for kept caches/connections as noted) need to be set again before performing a transfer.

functions.name: curl_easy_recv
functions.signature: CURLcode curl_easy_recv(CURL *curl, void *buffer, size_t buflen, size_t *n);
functions.description: Receives data from the connected socket associated with the easy handle. Use only after a successful curl_easy_perform() when the handle was configured with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY. Writes up to buflen bytes into buffer and stores the number of bytes received in *n.
requirements: curl must be a valid easy handle that has completed a successful curl_easy_perform() with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY enabled.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least buflen bytes.
n must be a valid pointer to size_t to receive the number of bytes read.
buflen should reflect the maximum number of bytes the caller is prepared to receive in this call.

functions.name: curl_easy_send
functions.signature: CURLcode curl_easy_send(CURL *curl, const void *buffer, size_t buflen, size_t *n);
functions.description: Sends data over the connected socket associated with the easy handle. Use only after a successful curl_easy_perform() when the handle was configured with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY. Attempts to send up to buflen bytes from buffer and stores the number of bytes sent in *n.
requirements: curl must be a valid easy handle that has completed a successful curl_easy_perform() with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY enabled.
buffer must point to readable memory of at least buflen bytes.
n must be a valid pointer to size_t to receive the number of bytes sent.
buflen specifies the number of bytes to attempt to send in this call.

functions.name: curl_easy_upkeep
functions.description: Performs connection upkeep for the given easy handle (e.g., to maintain or refresh underlying connections).
requirements: curl must be a valid CURL easy handle.

functions.name: curl_multi_init
functions.description: Create and return a new multi handle for managing multiple easy handles concurrently via the libcurl multi interface. Use the returned handle with other curl_multi_* APIs and destroy it with curl_multi_cleanup when done.
requirements: Must be called before passing the handle to any other curl_multi_* function.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check the return value before use.
The returned handle must later be cleaned up with curl_multi_cleanup.

functions.name: curl_multi_add_handle
functions.description: Add an easy handle to a multi handle so it can be driven by the multi interface for concurrent transfers.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM* returned by curl_multi_init.
curl_handle must be a valid CURL* created by curl_easy_init and configured as desired.
A given easy handle must not already be added to a (this or another) multi handle.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success or the specific error (e.g., CURLM_ADDED_ALREADY, CURLM_BAD_EASY_HANDLE).

functions.name: curl_multi_remove_handle
functions.description: Remove a previously added easy handle from the multi handle, stopping it from being managed by the multi interface.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
curl_handle must be a valid CURL* that is currently added to multi_handle.
Callers must check the returned CURLMcode to confirm successful removal.

functions.name: curl_multi_fdset
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_fdset(CURLM *multi_handle,
                                       fd_set *read_fd_set,
                                       fd_set *write_fd_set,
                                       fd_set *exc_fd_set,
                                       int *max_fd);
functions.description: Populate fd_set structures with the file descriptors libcurl is interested in for reading, writing, and exceptions, to allow applications to use select() alongside curl_multi_perform. Writes the highest file descriptor value into max_fd.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.

Any of read_fd_set, write_fd_set, exc_fd_set may be NULL if not needed; non-NULL sets must be initialized by the caller before passing to this function (common select() practice, not explicitly stated here).
max_fd must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the maximum fd value.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success before using the populated sets.

functions.name: curl_multi_wait
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_wait(CURLM *multi_handle,
                                      struct curl_waitfd extra_fds[],
                                      unsigned int extra_nfds,
                                      int timeout_ms,
                                      int *ret);
functions.description: Wait/poll for activity on file descriptors used by a multi handle, optionally including additional application-provided fds. On return, writes the number of fds with activity to ret.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
extra_fds may be NULL when extra_nfds is 0; otherwise it must point to an array of at least extra_nfds curl_waitfd entries.
timeout_ms is a timeout in milliseconds; range/semantics beyond that are not specified here.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the number of fds with activity.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_poll
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_poll(CURLM *multi_handle,
                                      struct curl_waitfd extra_fds[],
                                      unsigned int extra_nfds,
                                      int timeout_ms,
                                      int *ret);
functions.description: Poll for activity on all fds within a multi handle plus optional extra fds. Similar to curl_multi_wait; writes the number of fds with activity to ret.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
extra_fds may be NULL when extra_nfds is 0; otherwise it must reference at least extra_nfds entries.
timeout_ms is in milliseconds (further semantics not specified here).
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the count.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_wakeup
functions.description: Wake up a thread blocked in curl_multi_poll on the given multi handle, causing it to return early.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success (e.g., CURLM_WAKEUP_FAILURE indicates failure).

functions.name: curl_multi_perform
functions.description: Drive transfers for all easy handles in the multi handle. Processes any pending I/O and returns quickly. Writes the number of handles that are still transferring to running_handles.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
running_handles must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the number of active transfers remaining.
This function may be called even if no fds appear ready; callers should loop until running_handles reaches 0.
Check the returned CURLMcode for stack-level errors; individual transfer results must be retrieved via curl_multi_info_read.

functions.name: curl_multi_cleanup
functions.description: Clean up and destroy a multi handle. Does not free or alter individual easy handles that were added to it.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM* previously returned by curl_multi_init.
Do not use the multi handle after cleanup.
State of in-progress transfers on easy handles when called mid-transfer is not defined here; callers should remove handles or ensure transfers are complete before cleanup for predictable behavior.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_info_read
functions.description: Retrieve messages about completed or informational events for easy handles managed by the multi handle. Returns one message per call until no more are available, and writes the number of messages remaining to msgs_in_queue.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
msgs_in_queue must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the remaining count.
The returned CURLMsg pointer may be NULL if there are no messages or on failure.
The data pointed to by the returned pointer will not survive a subsequent curl_multi_cleanup on the multi handle.
For detailed information about a transfer, use the CURL* easy handle in the message with curl_easy_getinfo.

functions.name: curl_multi_strerror
functions.description: Convert a CURLMcode error value to a human-readable, null-terminated error string suitable for logging or diagnostics.
requirements: Input must be a valid CURLMcode enumeration value.
The returned pointer must not be modified by the caller; lifetime management is internal to libcurl (not further specified in this header).

functions.name: curl_multi_socket
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode CURL_DEPRECATED(7.19.5, "Use curl_multi_socket_action()")
curl_multi_socket(CURLM *multi_handle, curl_socket_t s, int *running_handles);
functions.description: Deprecated alternative to curl_multi_perform that lets the application tell libcurl which socket has activity so libcurl can perform I/O. Use curl_multi_socket_action instead.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
s must be a valid socket managed by the multi handle, or CURL_SOCKET_TIMEOUT to trigger timeout processing (via macro mapping when old API is disabled).
running_handles must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the number of active transfers.
Prefer curl_multi_socket_action for new code; availability of this symbol may depend on build options/macros.

functions.name: curl_multi_socket_action
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_socket_action(CURLM *multi_handle,
                                               curl_socket_t s,
                                               int ev_bitmask,
                                               int *running_handles);
functions.description: Notify libcurl that a specific socket has I/O activity and drive transfers accordingly. The ev_bitmask specifies which events occurred (e.g., CURL_CSELECT_IN, CURL_CSELECT_OUT, CURL_CSELECT_ERR). Writes the number of still-active transfers to running_handles.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
s must be a socket of interest to the multi handle, or CURL_SOCKET_TIMEOUT to process timeouts.
ev_bitmask is a bitmask of CURL_CSELECT_* flags indicating the event(s).
running_handles must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the count.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_socket_all
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode CURL_DEPRECATED(7.19.5, "Use curl_multi_socket_action()")
curl_multi_socket_all(CURLM *multi_handle, int *running_handles);
functions.description: Deprecated convenience to tell libcurl to act on all relevant sockets for the multi handle. Use curl_multi_socket_action instead.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
running_handles must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the active transfer count.
Prefer curl_multi_socket_action for new code.

functions.name: curl_multi_timeout
functions.description: Get the maximum number of milliseconds the application may wait before it must call curl_multi_socket_action or curl_multi_perform to allow libcurl’s timed events to run. Writes the timeout value to milliseconds.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
milliseconds must be a non-NULL pointer to long to receive the timeout.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_setopt
functions.description: Set an option on a multi handle. Options include callbacks, user data pointers, and limits (see CURLMoption enum).
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
option must be a valid CURLMoption value; the variadic argument(s) must match the expected type for the option (e.g., function pointer, object pointer, long, curl_off_t).
Passing an unsupported or mismatched option/value will return CURLM_UNKNOWN_OPTION or CURLM_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT.
Caller must ensure that any installed callback functions conform to the specified signatures and remain valid for the duration of their use.

functions.name: curl_multi_assign
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_assign(CURLM *multi_handle,
                                        curl_socket_t sockfd, void *sockp);
functions.description: Associate application-specific data (sockp) with a socket used by the multi handle, retrievable via the socket callback mechanism. Intended for use with the socket-based multi API.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
sockfd must reference a socket that libcurl uses for this multi handle.
sockp may be NULL or any pointer-sized value the application wants to associate.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_get_handles
functions.description: Return a newly allocated array of all easy handles currently added to the multi handle, terminated by a NULL pointer. If no easy handles are added, returns an array whose first entry is NULL.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.
The returned array is allocated; memory ownership and required deallocation method are not specified in this header (consult libcurl documentation).

functions.name: curl_multi_get_offt
functions.description: Retrieve a numeric value corresponding to a CURLMINFO_* query and store it in pvalue.
requirements: multi_handle must be a valid CURLM*.
info must be one of the CURLMINFO_* values defined by CURLMinfo_offt.
pvalue must be a non-NULL pointer to curl_off_t where the result will be stored.
Check the returned CURLMcode; an error indicates the value could not be obtained.

functions.name: curl_pushheader_bynum
functions.description: During an HTTP/2 server push callback, retrieve the Nth pushed header field by index from the provided push headers structure.
requirements: h must be a valid pointer supplied by libcurl within a push-related callback.
num is a zero-based index of the header to retrieve; valid range is not specified here.
The returned char* points to header data managed by libcurl; ownership and lifetime are not specified in this header (consult documentation).
Function is intended for use only within the context of the push callback.

functions.name: curl_pushheader_byname
functions.description: During an HTTP/2 server push callback, retrieve the value of a pushed header by its case-insensitive name from the provided push headers structure.
requirements: h must be a valid pointer supplied by libcurl within a push-related callback.
name must be a non-NULL C string naming the header to look up.
The returned char* points to header data managed by libcurl; ownership and lifetime are not specified in this header (consult documentation).
Function is intended for use only within the context of the push callback.

functions.name: curl_multi_waitfds
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_waitfds(CURLM *multi,
                                         struct curl_waitfd *ufds,
                                         unsigned int size,
                                         unsigned int *fd_count);
functions.description: Ask libcurl to provide file descriptors suitable for polling. Optionally pass a buffer to receive them; passing size zero allows querying only the count. Writes the number of fds produced to fd_count.
requirements: multi must be a valid CURLM*.
ufds may be NULL when size is 0; otherwise it must point to an array with capacity for at least size entries.
size specifies the capacity of ufds in entries; zero is allowed to just query the count.
fd_count must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of fds.
Check the returned CURLMcode for success before using ufds.

functions.name: curl_multi_notify_disable
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_notify_disable(CURLM *multi,
                                                unsigned int notification);
functions.description: Disable a specific notification type from being dispatched by a multi handle when notifications are enabled (via CURLMOPT_NOTIFYFUNCTION).
requirements: multi must be a valid CURLM*.
notification must be one of the defined notification constants (e.g., CURLMNOTIFY_INFO_READ, CURLMNOTIFY_EASY_DONE).
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_multi_notify_enable
functions.signature:
CURL_EXTERN CURLMcode curl_multi_notify_enable(CURLM *multi,
                                               unsigned int notification);
functions.description: Enable a specific notification type to be dispatched by a multi handle to a previously installed notify callback.
requirements: multi must be a valid CURLM*.
notification must be one of the defined notification constants (e.g., CURLMNOTIFY_INFO_READ, CURLMNOTIFY_EASY_DONE).
A notify callback should be installed beforehand via CURLMOPT_NOTIFYFUNCTION for notifications to be delivered (implied by option names; not explicitly enforced here).
Check the returned CURLMcode for success.

functions.name: curl_ws_recv
functions.signature: CURLcode curl_ws_recv(CURL *curl, void *buffer, size_t buflen, size_t *recv, const struct curl_ws_frame **metap);
functions.description: Receives data from a WebSocket connection on a CURL easy handle. Intended to be used after a successful curl_easy_perform() with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY to read WebSocket payload data. On return, *recv contains the number of bytes placed into buffer and, if metap is non-NULL, *metap points to metadata describing the current frame (opcode/flags, offsets, remaining bytes).
requirements: curl must be a valid, initialized CURL easy handle that has completed a successful curl_easy_perform() using CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY for a WebSocket connection (stated in header comment).
buffer must point to writable memory of at least buflen bytes (inferred from signature: void *buffer, size_t buflen).
buflen should be greater than 0 to receive any payload data (inferred from typical recv semantics).
recv must be a non-NULL pointer where the function stores the number of bytes actually received (inferred from signature).
metap may be NULL if frame metadata is not needed; if non-NULL, it must point to storage for a const struct curl_ws_frame* where metadata will be returned (inferred from signature and comment).
Caller should inspect returned CURLcode to handle success or errors (inferred from use of CURLcode).
May only be called when the handle is in a state ready for WebSocket I/O (i.e., after the handshake/upgrade via CONNECT_ONLY) (stated in header comment).

functions.name: curl_ws_send
functions.signature: CURLcode curl_ws_send(CURL *curl, const void *buffer, size_t buflen, size_t *sent, curl_off_t fragsize, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Sends data over an established WebSocket connection on a CURL easy handle. Use after a successful curl_easy_perform() with CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY. The flags select the WebSocket frame type/behavior (e.g., CURLWS_TEXT, CURLWS_BINARY, CURLWS_CONT, CURLWS_CLOSE, CURLWS_PING, CURLWS_PONG, CURLWS_OFFSET). fragsize controls fragmentation of the payload into frames.
requirements: curl must be a valid, initialized CURL easy handle that has completed a successful curl_easy_perform() using CURLOPT_CONNECT_ONLY for a WebSocket connection (stated in header comment).
buffer must point to readable memory containing at least buflen bytes to send (inferred from signature).
buflen should match the intended number of payload bytes to transmit (inferred from signature).
sent must be a non-NULL pointer where the function stores the number of bytes actually sent (inferred from signature).

flags must be a combination of CURLWS_* bits appropriate for the intended frame type; choose exactly one of CURLWS_TEXT or CURLWS_BINARY for data messages unless continuing a fragmented message with CURLWS_CONT (inferred from provided flag defines and WebSocket semantics).
If using control frame flags (CURLWS_PING, CURLWS_PONG, CURLWS_CLOSE), ensure payload sizes comply with WebSocket expectations; specifics not documented here (unknown exact limits).
fragsize determines the fragmentation size of frames; allowed range/semantics are not documented in this header (unknown specifics).
Caller must check the returned CURLcode and handle errors (inferred from use of CURLcode).

functions.name: curl_ws_start_frame
functions.signature: CURLcode curl_ws_start_frame(CURL *curl, unsigned int flags, curl_off_t frame_len);
functions.description: Buffers (starts) a WebSocket frame header with the given flags and total payload length on the CURL easy handle. It fails if a previous frame is not complete (e.g., its payload has not been fully provided). Use this to explicitly start a frame before providing payload data via subsequent send operations.
requirements: Calling this while a previous frame is incomplete results in an error (stated: "Errors when a previous frame is not complete").
flags must be composed from the CURLWS_* flag bits appropriate for the frame being started (inferred from "given flags" and defines).
frame_len should be the total intended payload length of this frame (inferred from "length").
curl must be a valid CURL easy handle already set up for WebSocket use; context implies usage after CONNECT_ONLY (inferred from being part of the same WebSocket API).
Caller must check the returned CURLcode and handle errors (inferred from use of CURLcode).

functions.name: curl_ws_meta
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current WebSocket frame metadata associated with the CURL easy handle. Useful for inspecting frame-related information (flags, current chunk length, remaining bytes, offsets) when receiving data.
requirements: curl must be a valid CURL easy handle participating in a WebSocket connection (inferred from context).

The lifetime/validity of the returned pointer beyond subsequent I/O calls is not specified in this header (unknown); callers should not assume it persists across further recv/send without consulting full documentation.
Caller should check for a NULL return to indicate lack of available metadata or an error (inferred from common pattern; exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: curl_easy_setopt
functions.description: Set an option on an easy handle. In this header, curl_easy_setopt is a macro wrapper around the real function that performs GCC static type checks when the option is a compile-time constant. The wrapper warns if the value type does not match the expected type group for the given option (e.g., long, curl_off_t, string, specific callback types, or pointers to specific libcurl structs). Use it to configure transfer behavior, callbacks, data pointers, and other settings on a CURL* obtained from curl_easy_init. Note: compile-time checks trigger only when the option is a compile-time constant; otherwise the call is forwarded without checks.
requirements: Must be called with exactly three arguments: handle, option, and value.
If option is in the long-argument range (0 < option < CURLOPTTYPE_OBJECTPOINT), value must be compatible with long (or int on platforms where long==int).
If option is an off_t option (((option) > CURLOPTTYPE_OFF_T) && ((option) < CURLOPTTYPE_BLOB)), value must be of type curl_off_t.
If option expects a C string (per curlcheck_string_option list), value must be a char*, signed char*, unsigned char*, or a char[]-like array.
If option expects a CURL* (CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS, CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E), value must be a CURL*.
If option is CURLOPT_RESOLVER_START_FUNCTION, value must be a curl_resolver_start_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_READFUNCTION, value must be a curl_read_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is one of the write-callback options (CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION or CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION), value must be a curl_write_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_IOCTLFUNCTION, value must be a curl_ioctl_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_SOCKOPTFUNCTION, value must be a curl_sockopt_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION, value must be a curl_opensocket_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_PROGRESSFUNCTION, value must be a curl_progress_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION, value must be a curl_xferinfo_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_DEBUGFUNCTION, value must be a curl_debug_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION, value must be a curl_ssl_ctx_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is one of the conversion callbacks (CONV_TO_NETWORK/FROM_NETWORK/FROM_UTF8), value must be a curl_conv_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_SEEKFUNCTION, value must be a curl_seek_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_CHUNK_BGN_FUNCTION, value must be a curl_chunk_bgn_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_CHUNK_END_FUNCTION, value must be a curl_chunk_end_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_CLOSESOCKETFUNCTION, value must be a curl_closesocket_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_FNMATCH_FUNCTION, value must be a curl_fnmatch_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_HSTSREADFUNCTION, value must be a curl_hstsread_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_HSTSWRITEFUNCTION, value must be a curl_hstswrite_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_SSH_HOSTKEYFUNCTION, value must be a curl_sshhostkeycallback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION, value must be a curl_sshkeycallback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_INTERLEAVEFUNCTION, value must be compatible with the documented interleave callback type (Wcurl_interleave_callback1/2) (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_PREREQFUNCTION, value must be a curl_prereq_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLOPT_TRAILERFUNCTION, value must be a curl_trailer_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is any of the *_DATA options listed in curlcheck_cb_data_option, value must be a pointer (any pointer type is accepted by these checks).
If option is CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER, value must be a char* or char[] buffer sized for CURL_ERROR_SIZE.
If option is CURLOPT_CURLU, value must be a CURLU*.
If option is CURLOPT_STDERR, value must be a FILE*.
If option is one of the POST fields options (CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS or CURLOPT_COPYPOSTFIELDS), value must be (const) void* or a character array/pointer.
If option is CURLOPT_HTTPPOST, value must be a struct curl_httppost*.
If option is CURLOPT_MIMEPOST, value must be a curl_mime*.
If option is one of the slist options (per curlcheck_slist_option), value must be a struct curl_slist*.
If option is CURLOPT_SHARE, value must be a CURLSH*.
Compile-time diagnostics occur only when the option is a compile-time constant; otherwise the call is forwarded without these checks.

functions.name: curl_easy_getinfo
functions.description: Query information about a transfer. In this header, curl_easy_getinfo is a macro wrapper that performs GCC static type checks on the output argument when info is a compile-time constant. It warns if the pointer type does not match the expected type group (pointer to char*, long, double, curl_slist*, curl_tlssessioninfo*, curl_certinfo*, curl_socket_t, or curl_off_t).
requirements: Must be called with three arguments: handle, info, and a pointer to storage for the result.
If info is in the string range (CURLINFO_STRING < info < CURLINFO_LONG, excluding CURLINFO_PRIVATE), the third argument must be a pointer to char* (i.e., char ** or compatible).
If info is in the long range (CURLINFO_LONG < info < CURLINFO_DOUBLE), the third argument must be a pointer to long.
If info is in the double range (CURLINFO_DOUBLE < info < CURLINFO_SLIST), the third argument must be a pointer to double.
If info is CURLINFO_SSL_ENGINES or CURLINFO_COOKIELIST, the third argument must be a pointer to struct curl_slist*.
If info is CURLINFO_TLS_SSL_PTR or CURLINFO_TLS_SESSION, the third argument must be a pointer to struct curl_tlssessioninfo*.
If info is CURLINFO_CERTINFO, the third argument must be a pointer to struct curl_certinfo*.
If info is in the socket range (CURLINFO_SOCKET < info < CURLINFO_OFF_T), the third argument must be a pointer to curl_socket_t.
If info is in the off_t range (CURLINFO_OFF_T < info), the third argument must be a pointer to curl_off_t.
Compile-time diagnostics occur only when info is a compile-time constant; otherwise the call is forwarded without these checks.

functions.name: curl_multi_setopt
functions.description: Set an option on a multi handle. In this header, curl_multi_setopt is a macro wrapper that performs GCC static type checks when the option is a compile-time constant. It validates value types for integer-like, off_t, callback pointers (notify, push, socket, timer), data pointers for callback user data, and char** where required.
requirements: Must be called with three arguments: handle, option, and value.
If option is in the long-argument group, value must be compatible with long.
If option is in the off_t group, value must be of type curl_off_t.
If option is in the data-pointer group (CURLMOPT_NOTIFYDATA, CURLMOPT_PUSHDATA, CURLMOPT_SOCKETDATA, CURLMOPT_TIMERDATA), value must be a pointer (any pointer type accepted by these checks).
If option is in the char** group (CURLMOPT_PIPELINING_SERVER_BL, CURLMOPT_PIPELINING_SITE_BL), value must be a char** (or compatible pointer-to-pointer to char).
If option is CURLMOPT_NOTIFYFUNCTION, value must be a curl_notify_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLMOPT_PUSHFUNCTION, value must be a curl_push_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION, value must be a curl_socket_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
If option is CURLMOPT_TIMERFUNCTION, value must be a curl_multi_timer_callback-compatible function pointer (or NULL).
Compile-time diagnostics occur only when the option is a compile-time constant; otherwise the call is forwarded without these checks.

functions.name: curl_share_setopt
functions.description: Set an option on a share handle. In this header, curl_share_setopt is defined as a pass-through macro that, for now, only enforces that the function is called with three arguments; no additional type checking is performed here.
requirements: Must be called with exactly three arguments: share, opt, and param.

functions.name: curl_strequal
functions.description: Compares two C strings for equality. The exact comparison semantics are not documented here (e.g., case sensitivity), but historically this is a convenience helper for string equality checks within libcurl. Considered subject to future removal per header comment.
requirements: s1 must point to a valid null-terminated C string.
s2 must point to a valid null-terminated C string.
Return value should be checked to determine equality (nonzero vs zero).
Exact comparison behavior (such as case sensitivity and locale) is unknown from this header; do not rely on specifics.

functions.name: curl_strnequal

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# Data type: binary file data
# We need to generate a bytes buffer that will be written to a temp file and then
# consumed by fuzzer stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Target fuzzers:
# - fread(): opens filename in rb and reads size*nmemb up to 2048 bytes. Any bytes are valid.
# - curl_mfprintf(): opens filename in wb+ and writes formatted data; filename need not exist.
#   Our buffer is not used for this stub, but must remain a valid arbitrary file content.
# - curl_mime_filedata(): passes filename to curl_mime_filedata which will attempt to read it.
# Therefore, generating diverse yet valid file contents is beneficial for fread and curl_mime_filedata.
# Strategy: produce a seeded mixture of patterns and sizes, including:
#   - Small random binary blobs (various lengths)
#   - Highly compressible patterns (repeating bytes, ASCII ranges)
#   - Structured segments (length-prefixed blocks, pseudo-headers) though not required, harmless
#   - Include 0x00, 0xFF, and increasing/decreasing sequences
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_block(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes([b]) * length

def _ascii_block(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Printable ASCII with occasional newlines and nulls
    choices = [*(range(32, 127))]  # printable
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.02:
            data.append(0)  # nulls sprinkled
        elif rng.random() < 0.04:
            data.append(10)  # newline
        else:
            data.append(rng.choice(choices))
    return bytes(data)

def _sequences(length: int) -> bytes:
    # Increasing then decreasing sequences to exercise buffered reads
    inc = bytes([i % 256 for i in range(length // 2)])
    dec = bytes([(-i) % 256 for i in range(length - len(inc))])
    return inc + dec

def _length_prefixed_chunks(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Build several chunks: [u32 len][payload]
    out = bytearray()
    while budget - len(out) >= 8 and rng.random() < 0.9:
        max_pl = min(256, budget - len(out) - 8)
        if max_pl <= 0:
            break
        pl = rng.randint(0, max_pl)
        kind = rng.randrange(4)
        if kind == 0:
            payload = _rand_bytes(rng, pl)
        elif kind == 1:
            payload = _repeat_block(rng, pl)
        elif kind == 2:
            payload = _ascii_block(rng, pl)
        else:
            payload = _sequences(pl)
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(payload))
        out += payload
    return bytes(out)

def _maybe_compress(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes prefix with a small header then append zlib-compressed tail
    if len(data) < 32:
        return data
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        comp = zlib.compress(data)
        header = b'ZLB\x00' + struct.pack('<I', len(data))
        wrapped = header + comp
        # Ensure we do not exceed limit; if too large, return original
        if len(wrapped) <= _MAX:
            return wrapped
    return data

def _mix_segments(rng: random.Random, target: int) -> bytes:
    segs = []
    remaining = target
    # Always include a header with magic and size for determinism
    magic = b'BIN1'
    hdr = magic + struct.pack('<I', target)
    segs.append(hdr)
    remaining -= len(hdr)
    builders = [
        lambda n: _rand_bytes(rng, n),
        lambda n: _repeat_block(rng, n),
        lambda n: _ascii_block(rng, n),
        lambda n: _sequences(n),
    ]
    # Add some length-prefixed subchunks
    lp_size = min(remaining // 2, rng.randint(0, 512))
    if lp_size > 0:
        lp = _length_prefixed_chunks(rng, lp_size)
        segs.append(lp)
        remaining -= len(lp)
    # Fill remainder with a few varied segments
    while remaining > 0:
        seg_len = min(remaining, rng.randint(1, min(256, remaining)))
        seg = rng.choice(builders)(seg_len)
        segs.append(seg)
        remaining -= len(seg)
    data = b''.join(segs)
    # Post step: maybe compress tail to create mixed characteristics
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        tail_ratio = rng.uniform(0.3, 0.8)
        cut = int(len(data) * tail_ratio)
        head, tail = data[:cut], data[cut:]
        tail_c = _maybe_compress(rng, tail)
        data = head + tail_c
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a total size tailored to fread cap (<=2048) but allow up to 4096 for generality
    # Since fread caps read to 2048, ensure many outputs are <=2048; sometimes larger for other consumers
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        size = rng.randint(1, 2048)
    else:
        size = rng.randint(1, _MAX)

    data = _mix_segments(rng, size)

    # Ensure inclusion of bytes 0x00 and 0xFF at random positions to exercise binary paths
    ba = bytearray(data)
    if len(ba) > 0:
        ba[rng.randrange(len(ba))] = 0x00
    if len(ba) > 1:
        ba[rng.randrange(len(ba))] = 0xFF

    return bytes(ba)

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary buffer
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string) and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (path to a file
# whose contents are fuzz-provided). We generate a single bytes buffer that the
# harness will slice into parameters. Our goal: produce valid, interesting inputs
# for the specific stubs:
#  - fwrite: writes payload to a file opened with "wb+" and may read back.
#  - curl_mime_data: uses the whole string as in-memory MIME part data (<=1024).
#  - curl_mime_data_cb: uses the string as a readable source via callbacks (<=1024).
#  - curl_easy_ssls_import: needs a key (C-string), shmac bytes, and sdata bytes (<=1024 each).
#
# Strategy:
#  We build a container buffer that concatenates a small header describing lengths
#  followed by segments:
#   [magic 4B] [flags 1B]
#   [payload_len 2B] payload bytes
#   [filename_len 1B] filename bytes (ASCII, no NUL, used by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME)
#   [mimeA_len 2B] mimeA bytes (<=1024)
#   [mimeB_len 2B] mimeB bytes (<=1024)
#   [key_len 2B] key bytes (ASCII, terminated with an extra NUL in stream to be safe)
#   [sh_len 2B] sh bytes (<=1024)
#   [sd_len 2B] sd bytes (<=1024)
# Total limited to <= 4096.
# The harness will split this buffer into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME calls.
# While we cannot control exact splitting, providing internally well-formed strings
# with embedded interesting byte patterns increases valid coverage across stubs.
#
# Content design:
#  - payload: mixture of printable text and binary patterns, including zeros, 0xFF runs,
#    and repeating sequences to exercise fwrite sizes and partial reads.
#  - filename: safe simple name with .bin extension; no directories to avoid path issues.
#  - mimeA/mimeB: short text-like and binary-like buffers for curl_mime_data and data_cb.
#  - key: URL-safe / token-like ASCII so key.c_str() is valid; ensure non-empty.
#  - sh and sd: random bytes up to 1024.
#
# Note: The fuzzer framework will consume bytes as needed; providing multiple rich
# segments maximizes the chance that each FUZZ_PARAM_* pulls a meaningful piece.

PRINTABLE = bytes([c for c in range(32, 127)])

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_block(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    L = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Mix of patterns
    if L <= 0:
        return b""
    # 1) ASCII phrase
    phrases = [
        b"Hello, world!\n", b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\n",
        b"text/plain", b"application/octet-stream", b"boundary=----libcurl-fuzz",
    ]
    parts.append(r.choice(phrases))
    # 2) zero run
    parts.append(b"\x00" * r.randint(0, min(32, max(0, L//8))))
    # 3) 0xFF run
    parts.append(b"\xFF" * r.randint(0, min(32, max(0, L//8))))
    # 4) incremental bytes
    inc_len = r.randint(0, min(64, max(0, L//4)))
    parts.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(inc_len))))
    # 5) random tail to reach length
    blob = b"".join(parts)
    if len(blob) < L:
        blob += _rand_bytes(r, L - len(blob))
    else:
        blob = blob[:L]
    return blob

def _safe_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    L = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if L == 0:
        return b""
    return bytes(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(L))

def _filename(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    bases = [
        "data", "payload", "mime", "upload", "ticket", "session",
        "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta"
    ]
    exts = [".bin", ".dat", ".txt", ".blob"]
    name = r.choice(bases)
    # add optional numeral
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        name += str(r.randint(0, 999))
    name += r.choice(exts)
    # ensure ASCII bytes
    return name.encode("ascii", "ignore")

def _bounded_len(n: int, max_allowed: int) -> int:
    return max(0, min(n, max_allowed))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Construct segments
    payload = _pattern_block(r, 16, 2048)  # fwrite payload also used elsewhere

    fname = _filename(r)
    if not fname:
        fname = b"out.bin"
    # Ensure no path separators to keep fopen simple
    fname = fname.replace(b"/", b"_").replace(b"\\", b"_")

    mimeA = _pattern_block(r, 0, 1024)
    mimeB = _pattern_block(r, 0, 1024)

    # key as visible ASCII token; ensure non-empty
    key = _safe_ascii(r, 8, 32)
    # Avoid whitespace-only; ensure alnum prefix
    if not key or not chr(key[0]).isalnum():
        key = b"K" + key

    sh = _pattern_block(r, 0, 1024)
    sd = _pattern_block(r, 0, 1024)

    # Enforce total size limit 4096 by trimming in priority order (least critical first)
    def total_size() -> int:
        # header sizes: magic(4)+flags(1)+ seven 2B lengths + filename len 1B
        return (4 + 1 + 2 + len(payload) + 1 + len(fname) + 2 + len(mimeA) +
                2 + len(mimeB) + 2 + len(key) + 1 + 2 + len(sh) + 2 + len(sd))

    # Trim helper
    def trim(buf: bytes, target_len: int) -> bytes:
        if len(buf) <= target_len:
            return buf
        return buf[:target_len]

    MAX_TOTAL = 4096
    # Gradually trim large segments if necessary
    for _ in range(10):
        sz = total_size()
        if sz <= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        # Choose a segment to trim, preferring sh/sd/mime blocks first
        order = ["sd", "sh", "mimeB", "mimeA", "payload"]
        for name in order:
            if total_size() <= MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            if name == "sd" and len(sd) > 0:
                sd = trim(sd, max(0, len(sd) - (sz - MAX_TOTAL)))
            elif name == "sh" and len(sh) > 0:
                sh = trim(sh, max(0, len(sh) - (sz - MAX_TOTAL)))
            elif name == "mimeB" and len(mimeB) > 0:
                mimeB = trim(mimeB, max(0, len(mimeB) - (sz - MAX_TOTAL)))
            elif name == "mimeA" and len(mimeA) > 0:
                mimeA = trim(mimeA, max(0, len(mimeA) - (sz - MAX_TOTAL)))
            elif name == "payload" and len(payload) > 0:
                payload = trim(payload, max(0, len(payload) - (sz - MAX_TOTAL)))
            sz = total_size()

    # Bounds for individual fields encoded as small integers
    payload_len = _bounded_len(len(payload), 2048)
    fname_len = _bounded_len(len(fname), 255)  # 1-byte length
    mimeA_len = _bounded_len(len(mimeA), 1024)
    mimeB_len = _bounded_len(len(mimeB), 1024)
    key_len = _bounded_len(len(key), 1024)
    sh_len = _bounded_len(len(sh), 1024)
    sd_len = _bounded_len(len(sd), 1024)

    # Header
    magic = b"CURF"  # marker
    flags = 0
    # flag bits could hint consumers to vary choices; include some random bits
    for bit in range(8):
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            flags |= (1 << bit)

    out = bytearray()
    out += magic
    out += struct.pack("B", flags & 0xFF)
    out += struct.pack(
        ">H", payload_len
    )  # big-endian 16-bit lengths for robustness
    out += payload[:payload_len]
    out += struct.pack("B", fname_len)
    out += fname[:fname_len]
    out += struct.pack(">H", mimeA_len)
    out += mimeA[:mimeA_len]
    out += struct.pack(">H", mimeB_len)
    out += mimeB[:mimeB_len]
    out += struct.pack(">H", key_len)
    out += key[:key_len]
    # add a NUL terminator byte after key to help any C-string usage
    out += b"\x00"
    out += struct.pack(">H", sh_len)
    out += sh[:sh_len]
    out += struct.pack(">H", sd_len)
    out += sd[:sd_len]

    # Final safety assert
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return bytes(out)

# Target data type: ASCII/UTF-8 NUL-terminated strings and filename-backed data.

# - URL escape/unescape inputs (including percent sequences)
# - Date strings for curl_getdate
# - HTTP headers for curl_mime_headers

PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

    "a", "A", "aaAA", "MiXeDCase", "straße", "CAFÉ",  # case-insensitive edge and UTF-8
    "hello", "Hello", "HELLO",

    "a%2Fb", "a/b", "name%3Dvalue&x%3Dy", "name=value&x=y",

    # WebSocket small payloads

    # Filenames (the harness will map FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to temp file path)
    "file.bin", "data.txt", "escape%20name.txt",
]

# Extra constructed strings
def random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def random_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with a few multi-byte UTF-8 sequences likely supported by curl/date parsing
    pool = [
        "é", "ü", "ñ", "ø", "ß", "Ω", "π", "你", "好", "🙂"
    ]
    s = []
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            s.append(rng.choice(pool))
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE))
    return "".join(s)

def percent_sequence_set() -> List[str]:
    seqs = []
    # Valid hex pairs
    for h in ["00", "09", "20", "2F", "3A", "41", "5A", "61", "7A", "7E", "FF"]:
        seqs.append("%" + h)
    # Mixed into texts
    seqs += ["test%20case", "%C3%A9", "%E4%BD%A0%E5%A5%BD"]
    return seqs

PERCENT_STRINGS = percent_sequence_set()

DATE_STRINGS = [
    "Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 GMT",
    "Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT",
    "Fri, 13 Feb 2009 23:31:30 GMT",
    "01-02-2003 04:05:06",
    "Tue, 15 Nov 1994 08:12:31 GMT",
]

HEADER_STRINGS = [
    "Accept: */*",
    "Content-Length: 0",
    "Expect: 100-continue",
    "X-Header: value",
]

# Compose a corpus with NUL separators so the harness can read N strings in order.
# Include duplicate entries to exercise self-comparisons.

def build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Pairs for strcasecmp/strncasecmp properties
    s = random_ascii(rng, 0, 32)
    out += [s, s]

    # Case-different pair
    t = "".join(ch.upper() if i % 2 else ch.lower() for i, ch in enumerate("CaseFoldTarget"))
    out += [t.lower(), t.upper()]

    # Known constants
    out += CASES

    # Percent sequences
    out += PERCENT_STRINGS

    # Dates
    out += DATE_STRINGS

    # Headers
    out += HEADER_STRINGS

    # Random ascii/utf8 samples
    for _ in range(10):
        out.append(random_ascii(rng, 1, 40))
    for _ in range(6):
        out.append(random_utf8(rng, 1, 30))

    # Short strings for widths/precisions
    out += ["short", "loooooooooong", "1234567890"]

    # Ensure some strings without ':' for header appender to extend
    out += ["NoColonHere", "AlsoNoColon"]

    # Filenames-like
    out += ["tmp.dat", "notes.md", "a/b/c.txt", "..%2Fsecret"]

    # Deduplicate excessive empties while keeping at least one
    seen = set()
    final: List[str] = []
    for s in out:
        key = (s,)
        if s == "":
            if "__empty__" in seen:
                continue
            seen.add("__empty__")
            final.append(s)
        else:
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            final.append(s)
    return final


def pack_nul_strings(strings: List[str], max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    blob = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
        # Ensure each is NUL-terminated for C API consumption
        needed = len(b) + 1
        if len(blob) + needed > max_bytes:
            break
        blob += b + b"\x00"
    return bytes(blob)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strs = build_strings(rng)
    rng.shuffle(strs)

    # Place a few specifically crafted format strings near front to increase chance
    # they are picked early by stubs that choose among inputs.
    front = [
        "Hello % World",  # literal percent
        "Ints: %d %x %+d\n",
        "Longs: %ld %lld Unsigned:%u\n",
        "Str: %.20s END\n",
        "Ptr: %p End\n",
        "Width/Prec int:%*d float:%.3f\n",
    ]
    # Ensure they are present
    for f in front:
        if f not in strs:
            strs.insert(0, f)
    # And ensure some header-like strings with ':'
    headers_needed = ["Key: Val", "Another: Header"]
    for h in headers_needed:
        if h not in strs:
            strs.insert(0, h)

    data = pack_nul_strings(strs, MAX_TOTAL)
    return data

# Target data type: printf-style format string
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and various
# numeric primitives pulled from the fuzz buffer. We should provide a buffer
# that, when consumed by the harness, yields:
# - A safe, NUL-terminated printable format-like string for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# - A valid filename for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (path to a writable temp file)
# - Reasonable numeric primitives (unsigned ints, doubles) sprinkled after
#   the strings so selectors and widths vary but remain defined
# Assumptions about the harness input layout:
# - Typical FUZZ_PARAM-style harnesses read sequential slices from the input
#   buffer in the order they appear in the stub. We therefore encode, in order:
#   [len][string bytes][len][filename bytes][sequence of primitives]
# We keep sizes bounded (< 4096 bytes total) and ensure NUL-termination where
# needed.

# Helper to craft a safe printf-ish string covering common specifiers used in stubs
SAFE_FORMAT_SNIPPETS = [
    b"Hello %% World",                    # literal percent
    b"Ints: %d %x %+d\n",
    b"Longs: %ld %lld Unsigned:%u\n",
    b"Str: %.20s END\n",
    b"Ptr: %p End\n",
    b"Width/Prec int:%*d float:%.3f\n",
    b"A:%d B:%u",
    b"S:%.30s",
    b"Pct: %% Done",
    b"F:%.2f I:%d",
    b"Fixed %% string",
    b"Vals: %d %u",
    b"Str: %.25s",
]

# Build a filename that most environments allow opening for write.
# Since the harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() then fopen(path, "wb+") in cwd,
# use a simple relative name with safe characters.
SAFE_FILENAMES = [
    b"fuzz_out.bin",
    b"out.dat",
    b"tmp.log",
    b"fmt.txt",
]

def _rand_u32(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    return rng.getrandbits(32)

def _rand_double(rng: random.Random) -> float:
    # Generate finite doubles within a sane range
    sign = -1.0 if rng.getrandbits(1) else 1.0
    mant = rng.random() * 1e6  # 0..1e6
    exp = rng.randrange(-6, 7) # scale by power of 10
    return sign * mant * (10.0 ** exp)


def _encode_len_prefixed(blob: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 32-bit little-endian length followed by blob
    return struct.pack('<I', len(blob)) + blob


def _make_printf_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose 1-3 safe snippets with separators; ensure NUL-terminated downstream
    parts = []
    count = 1 + rng.randrange(3)
    for _ in range(count):
        parts.append(rng.choice(SAFE_FORMAT_SNIPPETS))
    # Insert small literal words occasionally
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.insert(rng.randrange(len(parts)+1), b" ")
    s = b" ".join(parts)
    # Limit length to 64 like the stub does
    if len(s) > 64:
        s = s[:64]
    return s


def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = rng.choice(SAFE_FILENAMES)
    # Occasionally add a short suffix to vary
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        suf = rng.choice([b"", b".1", b".2", b".new"]) 
        name = base + suf
    else:
        name = base
    # Keep small (<= 32)
    return name[:32]


def _pack_primitives(rng: random.Random, count_u32: int, count_double: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count_u32):
        out += struct.pack('<I', _rand_u32(rng))
    for _ in range(count_double):
        out += struct.pack('<d', _rand_double(rng))
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build the printf-style string for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    fmt = _make_printf_string(rng)
    # Ensure NUL termination in consumer by explicitly appending a NUL in the stored blob
    fmt_blob = fmt + b"\x00"

    # Build the filename for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
    fname = _make_filename(rng)
    fname_blob = fname + b"\x00"

    # Pack primitives. Stubs consume several unsigned ints and doubles:
    # curl_mprintf: 6 x u32, 1 x double, 1 x u32 (selector)
    # curl_mfprintf: 2 x u32, 1 x double, 1 x u32 (selector)
    # curl_msprintf: 3 x u32, 1 x double, 1 x u32 (selector)
    # curl_msnprintf: 3 x u32, 1 x double, 1 x u32 (selector)
    # curl_maprintf: 2 x u32, 1 x u32 (selector)
    # Sum conservative upper bound to keep sequential consumption satisfied.
    total_u32 = 6 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 10  # extra slack
    total_dbl = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 + 4   # extra slack

    prim = _pack_primitives(rng, total_u32, total_dbl)

    # Assemble: [len][fmt][len][filename][primitives]
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _encode_len_prefixed(fmt_blob)
    buf += _encode_len_prefixed(fname_blob)
    buf += prim

    # Cap size to 4096 bytes
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

ZONEIDS = ["", "eth0", "en0", "zone%25id"]

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:

def build_full_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:

    path = rand_choice(rng, PATHS)
    query = rand_choice(rng, QUERIES)

def build_component_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    # Returns list of (label, value) for individual components.
    scheme = rand_choice(rng, SCHEMES)
    user = rand_choice(rng, USERS)
    password = rand_choice(rng, PASSWORDS)
    host = rand_choice(rng, HOSTS)
    port = rand_choice(rng, PORTS)
    path = rand_choice(rng, PATHS)
    query = rand_choice(rng, QUERIES)
    fragment = rand_choice(rng, FRAGMENTS)
    zoneid = rand_choice(rng, ZONEIDS)

    # Normalize zoneid to typical value (without percent), since curl may add encoding via flags
    zid_val = zoneid

    comps = [
        ("URL", build_full_url(rng)),
        ("SCHEME", scheme),
        ("USER", user),
        ("PASSWORD", password),
        ("HOST", host),
        ("PORT", port),
        ("PATH", path if path else "/"),
        ("QUERY", query),
        ("FRAGMENT", fragment),
        ("ZONEID", zid_val),
    ]
    return comps


def rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(L))


def interesting_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants = []
    # A few carefully crafted full URLs
    variants.append("https://example.com/")
    variants.append("http://user:pass@sub.example.com:8080/a/b?x=1&y=two#frag")
    variants.append("ftp://127.0.0.1:21/file.txt")
    variants.append("http://[::1]/")
    variants.append("http://[fe80::1%25eth0]/path?q=1")
    variants.append("file:///etc/hosts")
    variants.append("ws://localhost:80/chat?room=main")
    variants.append("https://xn--bcher-kva.example/search?q=b%C3%BCcher")

    # Randomly generated full URLs
    for _ in range(6):
        variants.append(build_full_url(rng))

    # Individual component samples (libcurl copies strings for set)
    comps = build_component_set(rng)
    for _label, val in comps:
        variants.append(val)

    # Edge cases for specific parts
    variants.extend([
        "http",  # scheme
        "",      # empty component to clear when used with set (still NUL-terminated here)
        "80",     # port
        "/%2Fleading-encoded",  # path with percent
        "a=1&a=2&b=3",  # multi query keys
        "frag-Section",  # fragment
        rand_token(rng, 1, 1),  # single-char pieces
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in variants:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq


def pack_cstrings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate NUL-terminated strings. Some fuzz harnesses split FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # by NUL; this provides many consumables.
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        # Ensure we do not embed NUL in the middle; replace if present.
        if "\x00" in s:
            s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
        b = s.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
        # Enforce total size bound
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += b + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = interesting_variants(rng)

    # Shuffle a bit but keep deterministic with seed; also ensure some critical
    # ones appear early: a valid https URL and an IPv6 w/ zoneid
    critical = [
        "https://example.com/",
        "http://[fe80::1%25eth0]/path?q=1",
    ]
    # Move critical to front if present
    ordered = []
    for c in critical:
        if c in strings:
            ordered.append(c)
            strings.remove(c)
    rng.shuffle(strings)
    ordered.extend(strings)

    buf = pack_cstrings(ordered)
    return buf[:MAX_TOTAL]

    # Choose one of multiple strategies to diversify behavior in curl_easy_header:
    strat = rng.randint(0, 9)
    if strat <= 5:
        # Frequently pick known/common headers
        base = rng.choice(COMMON_HEADERS)
    elif strat == 6:
        # Lowercase token (HTTP is case-insensitive)
        base = _random_token(rng, 3, 24).lower()
    elif strat == 7:
        # Uppercase token
        base = _random_token(rng, 3, 24).upper()

        parts = [_random_token(rng, 2, 8).capitalize() for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]

    b = name.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

    if not b:

    # Return within 4096 bytes constraint
    # Provide a terminating NUL to be friendly to C-string readers if used as-is.
    if len(b) + 1 <= 4096:

    else:

LOWER_IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _random_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 40, upper_only: bool = False) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = IDENT_CHARS if upper_only else LOWER_IDENT_CHARS
    # Ensure starts with letter or underscore
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase if upper_only else string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(L - 1))
    return first + rest


def _mutate_token(rng: random.Random, token: str) -> str:
    # Generate near-miss variants while staying syntactically token-like
    actions = []
    # Weight actions; more likely small case changes or underscores
    actions.extend(["lower_some"] * 3)
    actions.extend(["insert_underscore"] * 2)
    actions.extend(["delete_char"] * 2)
    actions.extend(["replace_char"] * 2)
    actions.extend(["suffix_num"])
    actions.extend(["prefix_junk"])
    action = rng.choice(actions)

    s = token
    if action == "lower_some":
        s = ''.join(c.lower() if (c.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.3) else c for c in s)
    elif action == "insert_underscore" and len(s) < 200:
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + "_" + s[pos:]
    elif action == "delete_char" and len(s) > 1:
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(s) - 1)
        s = s[:pos] + s[pos+1:]
    elif action == "replace_char" and len(s) > 0:
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(s) - 1)
        c = rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS)
        s = s[:pos] + c + s[pos+1:]
    elif action == "suffix_num":
        s = s + "_" + str(rng.randint(0, 999))
    elif action == "prefix_junk":
        junk = _random_identifier(rng, 2, 6, upper_only=True)
        s = junk + "_" + s
    return s


def _generate_candidate(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide the kind of token to produce
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.55:
        # Produce a known valid CURLOPT_* to trigger hits
        tok = rng.choice(CURLOPT_NAMES)
        # Sometimes return exactly, sometimes a mild variant that still matches formatting in stub
        if rng.random() < 0.75:
            return tok
        # Case flip or add harmless underscores (still valid in lookup? Keep it exact most of time)
        return tok
    elif p < 0.75:
        # Near-miss of a known option
        base = rng.choice(CURLOPT_NAMES)
        return _mutate_token(rng, base)
    elif p < 0.9:
        # Other families: invalid for this API but syntactically similar
        pref = rng.choice(OTHER_TOKEN_PREFIXES)
        return pref + _random_identifier(rng, 3, 24, upper_only=True)
    else:
        # Random identifier; sometimes with CURLOPT_ prefix constructed randomly
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            core = _random_identifier(rng, 3, 30, upper_only=True)
            return "CURLOPT_" + core
        return _random_identifier(rng, 3, 40, upper_only=True)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a small corpus of candidates; FUZZ_PARAM_STR may read one buffer entirely as a single string.
    # The stub only reads one std::string from FUZZ_PARAM_STR; therefore, we return exactly one token string
    # terminated by NUL to behave as a C-string when code expects c_str().
    token = _generate_candidate(rng)

    # Ensure maximum length respected by stub (<=256). Keep within limit and below 4096 total.
    max_len = 256
    if len(token) > max_len:
        token = token[:max_len]

    # Provide as bytes with an explicit NUL terminator to ensure well-formed C string semantics
    data = token.encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"

    # As a minor variation, occasionally append another NUL-terminated alias variant after the first.
    # Some fuzz harnesses may read more than one string from the same buffer; safe to include small extras,
    # but remain within 4096 bytes.
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        alt = _mutate_token(rng, token)
        alt = alt[:max_len]
        data += alt.encode('ascii', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"

    # Guarantee size bound
    return data[:4096]
